WILL NOT DO -- correct by design. Closing per your ruling on the Right Thing, with the reasoning rather than a cost argument.

The bead: pkix-chain::Error has variants wrapping upstream error types (Path, Revocation, Identity, Aia, Dane, PathBuild -- six now, the bead said five), so a breaking change upstream becomes one here.

That coupling is real and it is also total already, independent of the error type. pkix-chain takes pkix-path types in every public signature -- verify_chain(chain: &[Certificate], anchors: &[TrustAnchor], policy: &ValidationPolicy, ...) -- and it re-exports the upstream crates THEMSELVES: `pub use pkix_aia::{self, ...}`, `pub use pkix_path::{...}`, `pub use pkix_path_builder;`, `pub use pkix_revocation::{self, ...}` (lib.rs:111-124). A caller can write pkix_chain::pkix_path::Error today.

So insulating one error type while re-exporting the crate that defines it, and while demanding its ValidationPolicy and TrustAnchor on every call, would be incoherent -- not a smaller version of the fix, but an inconsistency. To make the insulation mean anything you would have to re-wrap the whole vocabulary.

Which is exactly what pkix-chain-simple is: "Strict, opinionated X.509 chain verifier for the common happy-path case", with eight purpose-built error variants of its own. The layering is already correct -- pkix-chain shares the vocabulary deliberately, pkix-chain-simple narrows it. PKIX-rm8.23 stays open because that crate has ONE Path(PathError) passthrough that undercuts its own design, and there the bead argument does land.

Callers also lose nothing here: the wrapped variants let them match all the way down to the specific validation failure, which is what a PKI consumer needs to decide between "expired", "revoked", "name mismatch" and "untrusted root".

See also PKIX-sqek.27, closed with the same reasoning, and PKIX-sqek.25, which is the same question asked about the re-exports themselves.
